 Tops still have goals to reach against Jax State
 Published 10:05 am Friday, November 13, 2026
 By Jeff Nations

 A spot in the Conference USA championship game is out of reach for Western Kentucky.
 Middle Tennessee put that slim possibility to rest by dealing the Tops a 51-42 loss last week in Murfreesboro, Tennessee.
 WKU (3-6 overall, 2-3 CUSA), the preseason pick to win the league title in the coaches’ poll, won’t be hoisting the trophy this season. But with three games left to play in the regular season, the Tops still have plenty to play for starting with a Homecoming matchup against co-CUSA leader Jacksonville State at 2:30 p.m. on Saturday at Houchens-Smith Stadium.
 There’s still the potential for a bowl bid, for one – WKU has earned a bowl bid in each of head coach Tyson Helton’s seven seasons leading the program, winning five.
 Avoiding a losing record by winning the last three to finish .500 is another source of motivation.
 “A lot of ups and downs, you know, bringing us together more so,” WKU graduate senior linebacker Jaylen Wester said. “Right now how we’re just feeling, take every game one-by-one. Everything’s ahead of us, like coach Helton has been telling us. Everything’s ahead of us. We still have a bright future. We still can finish strong. So we’ve got to put everything that was in the past to bed, and focus on Jax State because it’s the next game.”

 Jacksonville State (7-2 overall, 5-0 CUSA) enters Saturday’s matchup on a six-game winning streak after trouncing visiting Sam Houston 47-14 last week. The Gamecocks are trying to keep pace with CUSA co-leader Liberty. Those two teams don’t play in the regular season, but appear headed toward a matchup in the CUSA championship next month.
 Jax State quarterback Caden Creel is a proven dual-threat menace. Creel ranks second in CUSA in rushing with 800 yards and six touchdowns and is more than capable of doing damage with his arm as well (1,987 passing yards and 15 touchdowns). Creel has been a bit susceptible on turnovers with eight interceptions this season.
 “If you want to go win the game against Jacksonville State, you have to contain their quarterback and that’s hard to do,” Helton said. “That’s a big challenge, but we’ve got to go out there and do it. And I have belief in our defense and our defensive players that we can go do that. Good players are going to make their plays, but you’ve got to try in critical times to come up with a big sack or try to create a turnover or have great coverage when the ball goes down the field and make a play on it. You’ve got to go take advantage of those opportunities.”
 The Tops have been vulnerable to big plays on defense all season – WKU currently ranks last in the league in scoring defense (33.3 points allowed).
 WKU’s offense nearly matched the Blue Raiders in total yardage (513-497) just as the Tops did the previous week in a home loss to Delaware, but finishing with points has been more of a struggle. The Hilltoppers are just seventh in CUSA in scoring offense (23.6 points per game) and are going up against the league’s second best scoring defense in Jax State (19.2 points allowed per game).
 “At times we’re playing some really good defense, doing some really good things,” Helton said. “But you look at the first play of the second half, they pop a long touchdown right off the bat. We’ve had a couple of those and those can’t happen, especially when you play a good football team. So we have to clean those up. We can’t just give them an easy touchdown like that. So that’s one area. And then offensively … you know, offense is a battle to finish drives and then put the ball in the end zone. And that was really a point of emphasis for us last week – it is every week, but we were able to go do that particularly in the second half.”
 WKU got a lift from quarterback Rodney Tisdale Jr. in last week’s game at MTSU. When Brock Glenn was sidelined late after getting poked in the eye, Tisdale – the season-opening starter who has been out of the lineup with ankle injuries – came on in relief and led the Tops on two fourth-quarter touchdown drives that tied the game at 42-all with just 31 seconds to play.
 Helton said during Monday’s news conference it was too early to tell if Glenn would be available for starting duties, but he expects both quarterbacks to be available.
 “Nothing changes – both those guys get reps,” Helton said. “We try to build the game plan around both those guys.”
 WKU leads the all-time series against Jax State 5-4 and has won all four meetings at Houchens-Smith Stadium. The Gamecocks have won the last two, including a matchup in the 2024 CUSA championship. Saturday’s game will be streamed on ESPN+.
 “The biggest thing is focus on us and focus on the game at hand and beating Jacksonville State,” Helton said. “And you take it one game at a time – I say that all the time, don’t look past that. We need to keep the blinders on and just keep looking forward. We should be excited to come home and play in this game. It’s a competitive game. The last time we were here it was a great game and I expect to have another great game with a big win.”
